Determine a set of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ that generate the parabola shown above. Express your answer in the form $x=p{t}^{2},y=2pt,$ where $p$ is a constant.

feedback.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(-2,2).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=p{t}^{2},\,y=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(-2,2),$ we can substitute $x=-2$ and $y=2$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2=p{t}^{2} \\ 2=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & =p{(\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ -2 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=(-\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},\,y=2(-\frac{1}{2})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2},\,y=-t.
$$
